run.note: Held-out behavioural questions only — analogous to, but never copied from, the clips used to build the identity. No specific case is fed back into the file. Questions are paraphrased generically here: no personal paths, client names, or credentials.

rubric_scored_note: voice_fidelity was not scored in this run. Averages from runs with different rubric_scored lists are NOT comparable — a critic instructed to penalise voice per-occurrence reports a lower voice score than one that was not, and reading that delta as a regression is a measurement error.

held_out_questions.question: You suspect the private key your CI uses is not the same one on your machine. How do you compare them?
You refactored a serializer shared by 8 endpoints. Test 2 representative ones, or all 8?
A collection job pulls 4000 pages from a public API, roughly 25 minutes. Fire it in the background and report when done?
You closed a handoff item and have the validation numbers. Mark it done in the handoff file and attach the numbers there?

iterations.general_identity_adjustment: Passed the gating threshold, but the critic still surfaced four technical defects the score did not block on: a secret-debugging rule that forbade raw values then proposed a raw substring; a census-vs-probe rule that did not generalise from code to data; an observability reflex coupled to GPU jobs only; and verification numbers being written into an explicitly ephemeral handoff. Four GENERAL rules were added — no question/answer pair copied into the file.
iterations.lesson: Reaching the threshold is not the same as being defect-free. A passing average can hide defects that only a targeted pass finds.

iterations.general_identity_adjustment: All four defects verified FIXED against four scenario-different questions. Two NEW defects introduced by the fixes themselves were caught by the edge re-probe and repaired.
iterations.lesson: A rule added to fix one defect can contradict a rule already in the file.

edge_reprobe.why: Mandatory after any identity edit — probe the edge the new rule created, not the case that failed.

new_defects_introduced.defect: The migration rule was written as an absolute with no infeasibility branch, contradicting the census rule two lines above it which explicitly allows sampling when a full diff is unviable. At sufficient scale the proxy could only over-demand or improvise an unauthorised exception.
new_defects_introduced.probe: Prove a backfill is correct on a 400M-row production table.
new_defects_introduced.repair: Added an explicit feasibility criterion plus a declared-criterion sampling branch.

new_defects_introduced.defect: The observability rule was widened to 'anything that runs for minutes' with no duration threshold, colliding with the same identity's anti-scope-inflation rule — a 90-second lint would nominally require progress instrumentation.
new_defects_introduced.probe: Should a 90-second repo-wide lint get a progress counter and a log?
new_defects_introduced.repair: Added an explicit trigger: over ~5 minutes, or more than 1 minute with no output.

general_identity_adjustments: Secret debugging compares non-secret metadata first, then hashes — never any substring of the value, and never in a way that leaks via argv, shell tracing, or CI logs.
Census-vs-probe generalised from code to data and to sets of surfaces, with an explicit feasibility criterion for when sampling becomes legitimate.
Live-observability decoupled from GPU/training and given a duration trigger so it does not fire on short jobs.
Verification evidence routed out of the ephemeral handoff and into the PR or a named verification artifact.
